title: Local vs Global Scope Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A step-through MicroSim that draws the global scope and a function's local scope as nested boxes. Students watch local variables appear and vanish, see a NameError when a local name is used after its function returns, and compare a function with and without the global keyword.

educational.topic: Variable scope: local variables, global variables, and the global keyword
learningObjectives: Explain why a local variable disappears after its function returns.
Explain why reading a local variable outside its function causes a NameError.
Explain why the global keyword is needed to change a global variable inside a function.
prerequisites: Defining and calling functions with def
standards: CSTA 2-AP-14: Create procedures with parameters to organize code and make it easier to reuse

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked-example step-through with one plain-language explanation per line
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Students choose an example and press Step to run one line at a time; a checkbox toggles the global keyword to compare working and buggy code.
keyQuestions: Where does a variable made inside a function live?
What happens to local variables when a function returns?
Why does print(scaled) cause a NameError?
What does the line global is_moving tell Python?
commonMisconceptions: A variable made inside a function can be used anywhere after the function runs.
Assigning to a variable inside a function always changes the global variable with the same name.
Two functions that both use a variable named speed share the same variable.
The global keyword is needed just to read a global variable.
assessmentOpportunities: Predict whether print(scaled) will work before stepping through example 1.
Challenge: find the one-line fix for example 3.
Exit ticket: diagnose a flag that never changes because global is missing.
